column1: # Getting those two rows to parse took four readings, and the lesson is the
# tree's own: A RECORD COUNT SAYS NOTHING ABOUT WHETHER THE FIELDS PARSED.
# The first run reported 835 records and rc=0 with every field named `col6` and
# the workbook's TITLE BLOCK stored as supervised banks. Three things had to be
# measured rather than reasoned about:
#   * the header is not row 1 — sheet row 12 on SIs, row 8 on LSIs — and
#     csv_skip_lines counts PHYSICAL lines, so the header's own quoted "\r\n"
#     (the cell reads "LEI / MFI code for branches") makes it span two of them;
#   * the two sheets of ONE workbook have DIFFERENT geometry: the LEI is col2
#     and the name col11 on SIs, col1 and col9 on LSIs. Declaring the SIs
#     positions on the LSIs sheet emitted 2,166 records titled by their LEI and
#     two shape notices saying 0 of 2,166 carried the declared keys — the
#     engine catching it, not me;
#   * and the header must not be read as a header at all. Its names live in
#     MERGED cells, so most are empty, and depending on which row the skip
#     landed on the parser alternated between positional `colN` names and a
#     field literally named "". `csv_no_header = 1` makes it deterministic,
#     which is the correct declaration for a spreadsheet laid out for humans.
